text.p: Speculative buying reignited this year's rally in world coffee prices and buying by funds also helped lift crude oil and metals markets. Gold firmed, helped by a weak dollar, but wheat bucked the trend and slipped quite sharply.
Metals made some steady gains on the London Metal Exchange, with copper and aluminium shining.
Three-months copper charged higher, fuelled by widespread buying, to peak at $2,415 per tonne in the afternoon before ending the session at $2,409, a gain of $19.
"Everything's looking very positive," said analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff.
Many in the market were emboldened after funds showed confidence by borrowing to roll over large positions last week, Adams said.
A fall of 1,750 tonnes in LME-supervised copper stocks, the first in about a week, lent support, while the weaker dollar sparked interest in non-dollar markets.
Aluminium skated to a high of $1,679, but forward selling pushed it back to $1,670 by the close, an $8 gain.
"We will see continued producer forward selling into the strength, but the fundamentals are looking quite good," he said.
The other metals were left behind and strayed little from recent ranges.

NYMEX crude features surged more than $1 a barrel by late Monday, boosting refined products futures to fresh highs shortly before the close. June crude oil futures reached a peak at $21.55 a barrel, up $1.12 on the day, before slipping slightly back, supported by renewed tensions in the Middle East. At 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, June crude was up 98 cents at $12.48 a barrel, while June heating oil was up 2.13 cents at 56.65 cents a gallon and June gasoline was up 1.41 cents at 64.25 cents a gallon. No supply disruptions were noted, but there was enough bullish news to lift the market through technical targets, attracting strong buying interest. Two major crude oil suppliers, Iran and Colombia, suffered earthquakes over the weekend, though there was no news of actual damage to oil production.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Monday, after gold, silver and the platinum metal group (PGM) all rallied strongly early, but the strength of the PGM's would continue to provide support for the rest of the complex, analysts said.

COMEX June gold ended down 60 cents at $348.70 an ounce, but not before climbing to its highest intraday level since April 8 at $352.20. The move back above $350 in June gold was forcing more fund shortcovering, analysts said, after COMEX gold open interest fell a further 990 lots Friday to 163,358 contracts, reflecting liquidation by funds last week.

But, after seeing a four year low around $337.00 in January, spot gold prices have found support again in the past few weeks around $340 an ounce, suggesting the low for year may be already in, analysts said.

Spot gold ended quoted $347.40/90 an ounce, after seeing an intraday high around $350.90, compared to the New York close Friday around $347.80/30. In London gold fixed at $348.20 Monday afternoon, the highest fix for a month.

The latest CFTC Commitment of Traders data, released late Friday, showed funds were heavily net short by 40,009 lots as of May 6, compared to a net short position of 37,500 contracts two weeks earlier.

CBOT wheat futures closed lower on a collapse in soybean futures plus bearishness stemming from USDA's projection for 1996-97 U.S. wheat carryover at 465 million bushels. Analysts had expected the government to place the carryover at roughly 450 million bushels. Wheat futures closed two to 14-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down 12 cents at $3.93 per bushel. New crop July was 14-3/4 cents lower at $3.99.
